title: #lempicka #lempickamusical #tamaradelempicka #edenespinosa #amberiman...
transcript: Yesterday, I saw Lempicka on Broadway, a new musical based on the life of Polish painter Tamara de Lempicka played here by Eden Espinosa. The story covers a lot of ground, and is definitely interesting enough for a musical and it captures big emotions and ideas worthy of singing about. Some of the plot points are a little muddy but overall it really comes together at the end, and I thought Act II was really tight and leaves a great taste in your mouth. I also enjoyed the score which is very specific and very intense. Most of the songs I feel aren't very suitable for a standalone casual listen out of context, but they're quite well suited to this show. My one gripe with the score though is at times it's a little wordy and doesn't always allow space for Eden's vocals to soar to their fullest extent. On the other hand, the songs Amber Iman sings as Rafaela are so good and she nails them all. Her tone, vocal agility, and range is just astonishing — she stole the show for me. I found this production design beautiful, grand, industrial, and angular, and what I liked the most about the show is that it has a very distinctive sound, direction, and overall vibe, which is generally big, dramatic, and very queer. I think any show that has such a clear vision has the potential to be quite polarizing so I don't know if the show will appeal to everyone but I was into it and the production is undeniably impressive. With that another Playbill for my collection.
